summary: Proposal: 'The Long March'. No XP, levels, currency or bonfires (all cut by the owner, docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:4-8,96-97). Instead the pawn climbs the chess board's own ladder: it starts on rank 2 and each of six boss defeats (Captain, Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, King) advances one rank, ending on rank 8, the last rank, where promotion is offered and refused (docs/design/gdd.md:377; docs/design/full-gameplay-design-v2.md:795). Rank is a story ledger, not a stat. Player power stays almost flat (Courage 3, damage 1); what grows is the option space, in four layers: (1) seven verbs, each a chess rule the pawn borrows but never becomes: Wooden Sword, Pencil Thrust, Rule Step (Knight), In Passing (en passant), Chalk Path (child call, with Chalk Block), Eraser Guard (Rook), Free Step (the final rule break), unlocking at fixed story markers about 5, 12, 44, 52, 62, 82 and 108 minutes in; (2) equippable Rule Pages: the existing Book of House Rules entries gain a Margin cost and a rule-changing modifier, with a budget equal to rank minus 1 (the build layer, modelled on charm and shard systems); (3) Annotations, optional side-room rewards that change a skill's rule; (4) the child's Believe economy, refilled by courageous play rather than time. Every skill is one SkillDef .tres (a subclass of the existing AttackProfile) run by one generic SkillSystem, so the owner can add or retune a skill by touching one data file. The research base is ability-gated metroidvanias, Zelda's item-dungeon, Mega Man/Kirby borrowed powers, Nintendo's kishotenketsu teaching, Celeste's few-verbs-plus-forgiveness, charm/shard loadouts, Schreiber's power-versus-difficulty curves, Sid Meier's interesting-decisions test, and the chess rules for promotion, en passant, castling and check. About 30 web pages were opened in full; the rest were seen only in search summaries and are flagged in sources.

progression_models.model: Ability-gated world (Super Metroid, Hollow Knight, Ori, Death's Door)
progression_models.how_it_works: The world is a set of locks that only particular verbs open, so a boss or item reshapes the map. Practice from the sources: a new ability is first demanded in a very simple scenario (Super Metroid power-ups: https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/level-design-patterns-in-2d-games), after the level has shown a reachable-looking but blocked space (https://medium.com/@lorenzoardeni/from-metroidvania-to-ux-what-we-can-learn-from-game-design-classics-5d9f29d72649, search summary only). Mandatory abilities form the critical path and are kept separate from optional ones so nobody soft-locks; an ability should serve more than one purpose (traversal plus combat) and should make old rooms play differently (https://dreamnoid.com/articles/how-to-create-your-own-metroidvania). Hollow Knight gates areas with movement abilities and some bosses grant them (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollow_Knight); Team Cherry's Silksong comments show the studio now loosens strict power-up routing (https://www.gamesradar.com/games/action/hollow-knight-devs-highlight-a-big-difference-between-their-sequel-and-most-metroidvanias-the-players-choice-about-where-to-go-in-silksong-is-not-dictated-by-what-power-ups-you-currently-have/). Dead Cells uses permanent Runes that open previously blocked paths (https://mcvuk.com/development-news/when-we-made-dead-cells/).
progression_models.example_games: Super Metroid, Hollow Knight, Ori and the Will of the Wisps, Dead Cells (runes), Death's Door
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Curiosity and mild frustration at a visible blocked place, then an 'aha' relief when the verb arrives, then the pleasure of re-seeing known rooms with new power (mastery and competence).
progression_models.fit_for_us: PRIMARY model for the verb ledger. The hub locks are already authored as ability locks: Bookshelf (page bridge missing), Block Tower (block wall or ruler gate), Dollhouse (furniture barricade), Under-Bed (blanket shadow) at docs/production/act-1-opening-to-first-boss-flow-map.md:496-503. Implement each lock as a data field on the exit/gate marker (requires_unlock_id), matching the existing WorldState.player_unlock_ids store (scripts/world/world_state.gd:22).

progression_models.how_it_works: Each dungeon contains one key item, locks that need it, and a boss that uses it. The dungeon teaches the underlying idea before the item arrives and the item then expands that idea instead of adding an unrelated mechanic (https://thecolorandshapeofplay.substack.com/p/how-zelda-dungeons-prepare-you-for). Mark Brown's Boss Keys graphs reduce dungeons to key item, locks and backtracking (https://www.zeldadungeon.net/we-interviewed-mark-brown-of-game-makers-toolkit/, https://www.patreon.com/posts/how-my-boss-key-13801754, search summaries). A good boss involves the dungeon's key item (https://www.zeldadungeon.net/how-to-design-your-ultimate-dungeon-boss/), and the Wind Waker finale re-tests each item and boss in Ganon's Castle (https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Ganon's_Castle), both search summaries.
progression_models.example_games: A Link to the Past, Link's Awakening, Minish Cap, Wind Waker, Twilight Princess
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Steady competence ('I understand this tool'), then a payoff when the boss asks exactly what the dungeon taught; a late rematch gives pride in accumulated mastery.
progression_models.fit_for_us: Use as the DISTRICT TEMPLATE (Rest, Teach, Test, Twist, Boss, Shortcut as in docs/design/full-gameplay-design-v2.md:627-650) and copy the Wind Waker idea for the Under-Bed gauntlet: one room per verb before the Black King. Item placement stays a data choice because an unlock is a PlayerUnlockMarker; moving a verb earlier or later is dragging one node.

progression_models.model: Boss-power chain and borrowed abilities (Mega Man, Kirby)
progression_models.how_it_works: Defeating a boss gives you its power. In Mega Man each boss is weak to one weapon and no weapon dominates, in a rock-paper-scissors loop, and the player chooses the stage order (https://themmnetwork.com/2014/02/14/weakness-wisdom-a-look-into-mega-man-3s-weakness-chain/, https://videochums.com/article/mega-man-1-boss-order-weaknesses-guide). Kirby swallows an enemy and borrows its power, lost on damage or discarded (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirby_(series)).
progression_models.example_games: Mega Man 1-3, Kirby's Adventure, Hollow Knight (boss abilities)
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: The triumph of taking the enemy's identity; anticipation of what the next boss will give; agency from choosing the order.
progression_models.fit_for_us: This is the fiction behind the verbs: BORROWED RULES. The pawn takes a move from the piece it beats (Knight leap, Rook line) but never becomes that piece, which keeps the owner's ending (the pawn refuses promotion, gdd.md:377). It also supports the approved flexible order: Knight first, Bishop and Rook in either order, Queen needs both (docs/design/gdd.md:294-299), provided each district is solvable with only the earlier verbs.

progression_models.model: Skill trees and XP levelling (RPGs, Sekiro skill points)
progression_models.how_it_works: Points buy nodes in a branching tree. Design critiques: filler nodes that are small percentage bonuses do not change play; if players can unlock everything the tree is just a ladder (thesis summary: https://www.theseus.fi/bitstream/handle/10024/192256/Orava_Santeri.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y, search summary only; forum discussion: https://www.resetera.com/threads/trying-to-pinpoint-why-i-dont-like-skill-trees.1552384/). Choices only carry weight if the options differ in play, and respec cost sets how anxious or casual choices feel (https://designdive.substack.com/p/design-dive-20). Players often prefer a new power at a boss over an arbitrary XP number (ResetEra thread above).
progression_models.example_games: Witcher 3, Sekiro, Path of Exile, Rise of the Ronin, Skyrim
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Planned growth and ownership when choices are exclusive; pressure and fear of choosing wrong when they are not.
progression_models.fit_for_us: REJECTED as a structure: the owner cut levelling (docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:4-8,96-97), a 90-120 minute game has no room for a tree (docs/design/gp7-progression-pacing-spec.md:33-37 forbids stat grinding), and gdd.md:554 excludes statistical upgrades. Keep only its one valid idea, exclusive choices under a budget, via Pages and Margin.

progression_models.model: Budgeted loadouts (Hollow Knight charms, Ori Spirit Shards, Paper Mario badges)
progression_models.how_it_works: The player finds many modifiers but may equip only a limited number, so each build is a budget puzzle. Hollow Knight charms cost notches, capped around 11 (fan wiki via search summary: https://hollowknight.wiki/w/Charms), and Gibson says the system draws on Paper Mario (https://mcvuk.com/development-news/when-we-made-hollow-knight/). In Ori and the Will of the Wisps the fixed ability tree was replaced by Spirit Shards the player collects and equips; because no shard is mandatory some could be unusual (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/q-a-designing-the-gorgeous-metroidvania-i-ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps-i-). Shotgun King offers upgrades as positive/negative pairs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_King:_The_Final_Checkmate, search summary).
progression_models.example_games: Hollow Knight, Ori and the Will of the Wisps, Paper Mario
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Autonomy and identity: 'my build'; experiment-and-adjust satisfaction; each boss feels like a small puzzle of preparation.
progression_models.fit_for_us: Adopt for the BUILD LAYER: Rule Pages in the Book of House Rules cost Margin. The Book already exists as data (scripts/data/rule_entry.gd:1-20, scripts/data/rule_book.gd:1-12, resources/rules/*.tres); a page only needs a cost and a modifier list. Keep every page a rule change, not a stat bump.

progression_models.model: Run-based boons and meta-progress (Hades, Dead Cells, Slay the Spire)
progression_models.how_it_works: Hades gives small permanent-progress channels and treats story as a reward so a death still feels productive (https://www.tomsguide.com/features/hades-exclusive-interview-supergiant, search summary; https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/how-supergiant-weaves-narrative-rewards-into-i-hades-i-cycle-of-perpetual-death). Supergiant favours designs where players discover different successful playstyles and are nudged out of a comfortable combination (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/supergiant-s-fourth-outing-i-hades-i-introduces-a-more-mature-organized-dev-process). Dead Cells deliberately uses fewer, more impactful items after seeing a huge pool of weak items fail in Binding of Isaac (https://mcvuk.com/development-news/when-we-made-dead-cells/). Slay the Spire balances so every card has a place (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/learn-i-slay-the-spire-i-s-metrics-driven-approach-to-game-balancing-at-gdc-2019, search summary).
progression_models.example_games: Hades, Dead Cells, Slay the Spire
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Anticipation and surprise from variation, the reassurance that effort is never wasted, and narrative reward for persistence.
progression_models.fit_for_us: Do NOT adopt run structure (hand-authored rooms are the owner's direction). Borrow three ideas: narrative as reward (each verb ships with a Book page and a child line), fewer-but-sharper content (7 verbs and about 10 pages, not 40), and verbs that open shortcuts.

progression_models.model: Knowledge as progression (Outer Wilds, Tunic manual)
progression_models.how_it_works: The player's understanding is the upgrade. Outer Wilds has no stat upgrades and keeps nothing between loops except what you know (https://www.dualshockers.com/outer-wilds-emergent-gameplay-design-opinion/, https://medium.com/@claire.boeck.172/interview-with-alex-beachum-ba7e21ee5d17, search summaries). Tunic scatters manual pages, some teaching techniques, so finding a page can reveal a mechanic the player never tried (https://80.lv/articles/tunic-s-developer-on-creating-the-in-game-manual-full-of-mysteries, https://www.redbull.com/us-en/tunic-video-game-developer-interview).
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Discovery, the 'I should have known' click, and earned insight rather than granted power.
progression_models.fit_for_us: Near-perfect match with the existing Book of House Rules (docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:99-114). Make every enemy page show its telegraph shape and the amendment, and make equipped pages the bridge from knowledge to action.

progression_models.model: Few verbs, deep mastery (Celeste, Sekiro, Braid)
progression_models.how_it_works: Celeste builds its game from jump, climb and dash and generates depth by level layout and combinations, with generous forgiveness (jump buffering, wall-jump leeway) so the hard part is the plan, not the input (https://maddythorson.medium.com/celeste-forgiveness-31e4a40399f1, https://medium.com/@josephdiamond115/the-award-winning-level-design-in-celeste-c2acb315bf79, search summaries). Sekiro drops builds, makes enemy attacks telegraphed with specific counters, and uses a generous deflect window where a miss degrades to a guard (https://www.superjumpmagazine.com/the-art-and-science-of-sekiros-combat/). Blow's advice is to keep digging below the first idea of a simple mechanic (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/gdc-europe-i-braid-i-s-blow-proposes-a-new-philosophy-of-game-design, search summary).
progression_models.example_games: Celeste, Sekiro, Braid, Hollow Knight (pogo and dash)
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Mastery and flow: the pleasure of fluency with a small toolbox, plus pride in beating a plan you invented.
progression_models.fit_for_us: This is the CAP: seven verbs, fixed on dedicated buttons (no skill-slot juggling), with depth coming from enemy-shape combinations per district. Copy the forgiveness habit already in the repo (input buffer, gdd.md:98) for every new cast window.

progression_models.model: Intent-visible tactical grids (Into the Breach, Shogun Showdown)
progression_models.how_it_works: Enemy intent is shown in advance and the player's tools move, redirect or swap enemies so danger becomes a solvable puzzle (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_the_Breach). In Shogun Showdown a swap skill can redirect an enemy's strike onto different tiles, and upgrades come as tile and skill modifications (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shogun_Showdown). Subset's design postmortem stresses cutting features and constraints (https://gdcvault.com/play/1026333/-Into-the-Breach-Design, abstract only).
progression_models.example_games: Into the Breach, Shogun Showdown, Tactical Breach Wizards
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Clever-solver satisfaction: the feeling of outwitting a visible threat rather than out-reacting it.
progression_models.fit_for_us: The game already has the telegraph engine: enemies lock cells at telegraph start (scripts/ecs/systems/enemy_ai_system.gd:233) and test the hero's cell at resolve (line 270), with one attack token (line 232). Make skills answer shapes (line, diagonal, L, multi-cell charge) instead of adding damage.

progression_models.model: Chess-native progression (promotion, borrowed moves, en passant, castling, check)
progression_models.how_it_works: Promotion: a pawn reaching the far side must become a queen, rook, bishop or knight; queen is the common choice and underpromotion (usually to a knight) exists for tactical reasons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_(chess)). En passant is a pawn-only capture available for just the next move after a two-square advance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En_passant). Castling is a king-and-rook swap with strict preconditions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castling). Check forces one of three answers: capture the attacker, move the king, or block (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Check_(chess)). Conventional piece values (pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9) give a ready cost scale (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_piece_relative_value). Shotgun King shows that chess works best as a rules language transformed into a new fantasy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_King:_The_Final_Checkmate; the repo already notes this in docs/design/gameplay-reference-research.md).
progression_models.example_games: Shotgun King, the repo's own enemy bible (pawn diagonal, knight L, bishop diagonal lanes)
progression_models.emotion_it_creates: Delighted recognition when a rule the player half-knows becomes a power; poignancy when the obvious power (promotion) is refused.
progression_models.fit_for_us: Use as vocabulary, not as a rules engine: Rank 2 to 8 is the ladder; Rule Step is the Knight leap; In Passing is en passant; castling survives only as a Page that swaps you with your own Chalk Block; check survives as the stagger state of a Perfect Guard; promotion is the ending choice (refused). Piece values, compressed to 1/2/2/3/3, price Pages.

skill_design_principles: A skill must change a decision, not a number. Sid Meier's test: an interesting decision has a trade-off, fits the current game state, expresses play style, and has enough information to make (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/gdc-2012-sid-meier-on-how-to-see-games-as-sets-of-interesting-decisions); the repo already requires this (docs/design/gp4-skill-system-spec.md:9-10,41-46). Acceptance test per skill: name one situation where NOT using it is the correct play, and one situation only it solves.

One verb answers one chess threat shape, so no two skills are interchangeable: reach (Pencil, straight), relocation over obstacles (Rule Step, L), counter to multi-cell movers (In Passing), hold against lines (Eraser Guard), terrain (Chalk), freedom of geometry (Free Step, diagonal). Any proposed eighth verb must beat a shape the first seven do not.

Cap the verb count and get depth from combination and context, as Celeste does with three verbs plus level layout (https://medium.com/@josephdiamond115/the-award-winning-level-design-in-celeste-c2acb315bf79, search summary). Hard cap: 7 verbs on 5 action buttons (Strike, Skill A, Skill B, Guard, Call); In Passing rides on Strike and Free Step rides on the movement keys. gp7 forbids late-game verb inflation (docs/design/gp7-progression-pacing-spec.md:33-37).

Every limiter is a RULE the player can read, never a hidden number. Guard only blocks straight-line attacks; Rule Step needs a free landing and a 4.0 s cooldown; In Passing needs a 2+ cell mover beside you; Chalk needs a gap and Believe. This answers gp4's veto on spamming skills to ignore room and enemy rules (gp4-skill-system-spec.md:41-46) and the parry-design warning that a dominant parry replaces positioning (https://tigogardenofmadness.substack.com/p/parrying-action-and-reaction).

Two economies, one per fiction. The pawn's own rules use cooldowns or windows (readable, no attrition); the child's calls use Believe, which refills only through courageous play (hits landed, Perfect Rub, rescues), never by time. Cooldown-heavy rotations flatten tactics when many similar abilities share short timers (editorial summary: https://rpgcodex.net/forums/threads/gamasutra-against-ability-cooldowns.71874/), so keep only three timed verbs (Pencil, Rule Step, Guard lockout) and make them unlike each other. Refilling a resource from melee hits rewards aggression and is proven in Death's Door and Hyper Light Drifter (https://www.nme.com/features/acid-nerve-developers-david-fenn-and-mark-foster-on-making-deaths-door-3203321) and Hollow Knight's Soul (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollow_Knight).

Borrowed, never owned. Each verb is a chess rule written in the Book as 'original rule' plus 'amendment' (the existing RuleEntry fields, scripts/data/rule_entry.gd:14-17). The pawn borrows from the fallen piece (Mega Man and Kirby pattern: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirby_(series)) and stays a pawn, which keeps the ending intact (gdd.md:377).

Suffer first, then wield. Show the player the pattern as an enemy threat before they own it: the Armed Pawn pokes at 2 cells before you take the pencil, Knights leap before Rule Step, the Passant Wraith captures you in passing before you learn it. This matches the Zelda principle that a dungeon teaches the idea before the item (https://thecolorandshapeofplay.substack.com/p/how-zelda-dungeons-prepare-you-for) and Super Metroid's simple-scenario first use (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/level-design-patterns-in-2d-games).

Every verb has at least one traversal use AND one combat use, and opens a loop. Dreamnoid recommends multi-purpose abilities and recontextualising earlier rooms (https://dreamnoid.com/articles/how-to-create-your-own-metroidvania); the soulslike plan makes shortcuts the relief beat (docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:38-44). Examples: Rule Step crosses one-cell gaps (Toybox lid shortcut, v2:649) and escapes locks; Chalk bridges tears and flanks; Guard erases Rule Marks and holds lines.

Separate mandatory from optional verbs so nobody soft-locks (https://dreamnoid.com/articles/how-to-create-your-own-metroidvania). Mandatory (gate the critical path): Sword, Rule Step, Chalk Path, Eraser Guard, Free Step. Optional (alternatives and secrets only): Pencil Thrust, In Passing, Chalk Block. Rooms may require only mandatory verbs already owned.

Space the verbs and fill the gaps with micro-rewards. Schreiber: new toys should be spread out and power should rise in small steps with a larger jump at the end of each area (https://gamebalanceconcepts.wordpress.com/2010/08/18/level-7-advancement-progression-and-pacing/). A verb every 10-20 minutes; a Page, Annotation, Courage Shard or hub change between, about every 5 minutes.

Forgiveness windows are part of the skill spec. Celeste buffers and forgives inputs so difficulty comes from the plan (https://maddythorson.medium.com/celeste-forgiveness-31e4a40399f1, search summary); Sekiro makes a missed deflect fall back to a guard (https://www.superjumpmagazine.com/the-art-and-science-of-sekiros-combat/). Eraser Guard: pressing early is a safe block, pressing at the last moment earns the bonus; pressing late does nothing. The existing input buffer is 0.12 s (gdd.md:98).

Difficulty is personal: tune upward and downward by choice. Celeste's assist and B-side approach (https://www.vice.com/en/article/celeste-difficulty-assist-mode/, search summary) and Jenova Chen's flow model, where static difficulty fits few players and choice is embedded in play (https://cacm.acm.org/magazines/2007/4/5692-flow-in-games-and-everything-else/fulltext, search summary). The repo's DifficultyProfile already has telegraph, observe, recovery and movement multipliers (scripts/data/difficulty_profile.gd:5-8); expose them as assist options and add negative-cost Vow pages later.

Emotion is designed per unlock, not bolted on. Motivation research ties enjoyment to competence, autonomy and relatedness (https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/SDT/documents/2006_RyanRigbyPrzybylski_MandE.pdf, search summary) and Lazzaro's hard fun is fiero, triumph after real frustration (https://yukaichou.com/behavioral-design/4-keys-2-fun-part-1-4/; paper: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248446107_Why_we_Play_Games_Four_Keys_to_More_Emotion_without_Story). Each verb is paired with a boss that can be failed a few times, a choice (autonomy) and a relationship beat with the child or a rescued piece (relatedness). Narrative reward is itself progression (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/how-supergiant-weaves-narrative-rewards-into-i-hades-i-cycle-of-perpetual-death).

ONE generic skill pipeline, seven .tres files (ECS: components = data, systems = behaviour, entities = assembled). (a) scripts/data/skill_def.gd: class SkillDef extends AttackProfile (scripts/combat/attack_profile.gd already holds range_cells, damage, impact_delay, recovery, color, texture, get_target_cells) adding id (same value as the unlock id used by PlayerUnlockMarker and WorldState.player_unlock_ids), slot (strike|skill_a|skill_b|guard|call|context|move_mod), source (own|child), cooldown, believe_cost, trigger (press|hold|window_after_event plus event name and seconds), shape offsets (reuse AttackPattern's forward/right convention, scripts/ai/attack_pattern.gd:11-34), tags, effects, upgrades. (b) Effects are pure-data SkillEffect resources with a kind enum: strike_cells, leap_self, step_self, status_self, paint_cells, drag_target, interrupt_target, swap_with_marker. (c) New components in scripts/ecs/ecs_components.gd: SkillBook (unlocked ids, per-skill cooldown_left and applied upgrades), SkillCast (skill, phase, time_left, locked cells), Status (guard_left, untargetable_left, in_check_left), Believe, Margin (budget, equipped page ids), PassantWindow. (d) Systems: SkillSystem replaces CombatSystem (scripts/main.gd:112) and reads a SkillIntent written by PlayerInputSystem instead of AttackIntent.kind sword/skill (scripts/ecs/systems/player_input_system.gd:25-30, scripts/ecs/ecs_components.gd:65-67); HealthSystem._apply_damage (scripts/ecs/systems/health_system.gd:35-50) is the single damage choke point where Status is checked; enemy damage events (enemy_ai_system.gd:271-275) gain a tag copied from AttackPattern/EnemyWeapon data; TerrainSystem expires chalk; ViewSyncSystem publishes AnimationTree conditions; main.gd consumes events (skill_cast_started, skill_unlocked, believe_changed, page_equipped, rank_changed) for HUD and SfxManager. (e) Authoring cost: a new skill from existing effect kinds = 1 SkillDef .tres + 1 unlock marker; a new Page = 1 RuleEntry .tres (add margin_cost and modifiers) + 1 line in resources/rules/rule_book.tres; a new effect kind = 1 match arm in SkillSystem. Today scripts/main.gd:406-413 hard-codes wooden_sword and PlayerCombat has fixed wooden_sword/pencil_thrust fields (ecs_components.gd:70-83); replacing those with SkillBook is the main refactor. No addon is needed (Resource subclasses are the Godot built-in, per the research-first rule in CLAUDE.md).
teaching_pattern:
One cycle per verb, mapped to Nintendo's four-beat structure: introduce, develop, twist, conclude (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/the-structure-of-fun-learning-from-i-super-mario-3d-land-i-s-director; summarised for 3D World at https://mcvuk.com/business-news/publishing/video-nintendos-level-design-secrets-in-four-steps/). Hayashida says each stage keeps one clear concept and the third beat is a surprise. Super Metroid applies the same idea: a new power-up is first needed in a very simple, safe scenario (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/level-design-patterns-in-2d-games).

KI, SUFFER (antepiece): a safe or lightly threatened room shows the problem the verb will solve, with no text; an enemy or the child demonstrates it. One crayon mark at most; the child must not lecture (docs/design/nar1-story-outline-spec.md, child voice rules).
SHO, GET AND FORCE (acquire plus forced use): the verb is awarded at a PlayerUnlockMarker and used within 10 seconds in a zero-risk spot, ideally the shortcut home, so the first use is also the loop-closing relief beat (docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:38-44).
TEN, TWIST (test under a different shape, or invert): the next district uses it against a new threat or combined with an older verb; late twists strip it away (the Queen locks Believe, the King strips directions).
KETSU, MASTER (exam plus optional mastery): a boss that rewards cleverness over execution, an optional Annotation room, and the Under-Bed gauntlet (one room per verb, the Wind Waker rematch idea, https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Ganon's_Castle).

Default placement of the unlock: AFTER the boss (the Mega Man and Kirby borrowing). The boss then tests prediction and positioning with the tools the player already has, and the new verb is needed only in the NEXT place (the shortcut home, the next district). Deliberate exceptions, because the player's relationship to tools is the story: Bishop, the child performs the verb by script while the player watches, then hands over the crayon; Queen, the child's calls are locked for a phase; King, tools are stripped and then reborn as Free Step. Zelda item-first (verb mid-district, boss as exam) is a one-node switch, because an unlock is only a marker position; use it for Eraser Guard if Rook Warden phase 3 turns out to demand it (v2:427). Gates require only verbs already owned, so Bishop and Rook can be done in either order (gdd.md:294-299).

Per verb (room ids from docs/design/full-gameplay-design-v2.md and the Act 1 flow map):
- Sword: KI T1 shows the dead king and the path; SHO T2 pickup then a harmless target; TEN T3 first pawn clash makes the sword necessary; KETSU B1 Captain exam.
- Pencil: KI T4 Armed Pawn pokes at 2 cells (you suffer it); SHO pencil stub beyond it and a tack-switch across a one-cell hole; TEN Toybox K2 L-lanes where the straight lane is the only safe lane; KETSU optional Annotation 'Lead Tip' room.
- Rule Step: KI K1/K2 Knight leaps against you with a 0.9 s landing telegraph; SHO KB defeated, the lid shortcut has a one-cell track gap; TEN Bookshelf diagonals when you must hop an island gap; KETSU Dollhouse barricade and an Under-Bed gauntlet room.
- In Passing: KI the Passant Wraith captures you in passing in a Bookshelf passage; SHO the Page flips and a Charging Pawn lane lets you try it with no other enemy; TEN Rook charges also trigger the window; KETSU a Courage Shard guarded by a charger.
- Chalk Path: KI B3 Torn Page Bridge, the child draws it by script while you watch; SHO crayon handed over after BB, the shortcut home needs a 3-cell page tear; TEN Rook district gaps under line fire; KETSU Midpoint hub combined rooms (Block plus Path), then the Queen locks Believe for a whole phase.
- Eraser Guard: KI R1 training Rook in a corridor, R2 Ruler Bridge; SHO RB defeated, the ruler-gate shortcut needs a rubbed Rule Mark; TEN Dollhouse mixed court where diagonals ignore the guard; KETSU Under-Bed lanes plus rewritten tiles.
- Free Step: KI the Queen's defeat shows one scripted diagonal step; SHO FB phase 3 strips to Up-only and rescues restore directions; TEN the King rewrites tiles so only a diagonal cell is open; KETSU the final strike, then the Last Rank and the refusal of promotion.

proposed_progression.spine:
THE LONG MARCH. A chess-native, XP-free spine in four layers, driven by story markers and one flat power baseline.

1) RANK 2 to 8 (story ledger, not a stat). White pawns start on rank 2 and promote on rank 8 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_(chess)). Six bosses, six steps: Pawn Captain -> 3, Knight -> 4, Bishop -> 5, Rook -> 6, Queen -> 7, Black King -> 8 (the Last Rank). Rank = defeated boss ids + 2, read from WorldState (scripts/world/world_state.gd). The HUD shows a small rank badge; the Book records it. Nothing is grindable.

2) VERBS (the skill ledger, mandatory path): seven verbs, each a borrowed chess rule, earned at fixed story markers. Order and approximate minute: Wooden Sword (T2, 5), Pencil Thrust (T4, 12), Rule Step (Knight Captain defeated, 44), In Passing (Bookshelf, Passant Wraith page, 52, optional), Chalk Path (Bishop Oracle defeated, 62), Eraser Guard (Rook Warden defeated, 82), Free Step (Black King, 108). Chalk Block arrives at the hub Midpoint (about 84) after both Bishop and Rook.

3) RULES (build layer): Book of House Rules pages become equippable. Margin = rank - 1 (2 at the hub, 6 after the Queen). Pages cost 1-3 Margin using chess values compressed to 1/2/2/3/3 (pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_piece_relative_value). Players cannot wear everything, so Page choice, not stats, is the build.

4) THE CHILD (relationship axis): Believe (2 crayon segments) powers the child's calls and is refilled by courage (hits, Perfect Rub, rescues), so help is earned (gdd.md:229-235; gp5:14-18). The child's trust states form a parallel progression: notice (Act 1) -> whisper -> chalk (Bishop) -> block (Midpoint) -> hands-off (Queen) -> cut off (King) -> partnership (ending), matching the approved emotional arc (nar1-story-outline-spec.md:21-32).

POWER IS FLAT, OPTIONS GROW: Courage 3 and Strike damage 1 never change by default. Difficulty comes from threat shapes and telegraph timing already in data. Why this spine: it keeps the owner's 2026-07-28 cuts, passes the gp4/gp7 vetoes (the vertical slice needs only Sword, Pencil, Rule Step; unlocks are spaced; no grind) and gives the 'proper progression' the owner asked for on 2026-10-12 through verbs, pages, annotations and story state. Emotional arc by unlock: Sword = agency after loss; Pencil = defiance; Rule Step = lightness and pride; Chalk = trust; Guard = resolve; Midpoint = the child's confession and partnership; Queen = fear of losing help; Free Step = freedom; refused promotion = catharsis.

THE ENDING CHOICE: after the King falls the pawn reaches the Last Rank and the game raises a promotion prompt (Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, or 'stay as I am'). The first four are real options shown with the names of the pieces the pawn borrowed from; choosing one plays a short bittersweet epilogue line and returns to the prompt; 'stay' is the true ending where the pawn steps beyond the board (gdd.md:377-380; v2:795). Underpromotion in real chess is a tactical choice, not a lesser one (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_(chess)), which is why the options should not be shown as obviously wrong.

skills.name: Wooden Sword (Capture)
skills.chess_meaning: The pawn's one legal way to take a piece, shrunk to the cell in front of it. The baseline every other rule deviates from; no combo strings (gdd.md:111).
skills.rule: Slot: strike (Space or K, project.godot:63-68). Shape: 1 cell ahead (range_cells 1). Damage 1. impact_delay 0.07 s, recovery 0.30 s (scripts/combat/attack_profile.gd defaults). No cooldown, no cost. Cannot start while stepping or during another cast; a press during recovery is swallowed, not banked (combat_system.gd:19-37). Locks target cells at swing start and resolves occupancy at impact (combat_system.gd:59-63,74-86). Data: resources/attacks/wooden_sword.tres converted to SkillDef with slot=strike and requires unlock id wooden_sword (already the id used in main.gd:412).
skills.new_decision_it_creates: When to commit. The 0.30 s recovery is the price of every swing, so each swing is a read of enemy telegraphs: stand in a safe cell and swing, or wait. It is also the yardstick: every other skill must do something the Sword cannot (reach, relocate, counter, hold, reshape terrain).
skills.unlocked_where: T2_FallenSwordTile, PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=wooden_sword (already built: scripts/world/player_unlock_marker.gd:6-10, scripts/main.gd:416-423). About minute 5.
skills.story_beat: Agency after loss. The pawn picks up a weapon a cheating Black piece dropped (docs/production/act-1-opening-to-first-boss-flow-map.md, T2). The Book's first page states the unbroken law (resources/rules/first_law.tres).
skills.upgrades: None by design. Optional alternate Strike, the Ruler Blade (front cell plus both forward diagonals, impact 0.12, recovery 0.45), found in the Block Tower yard and swapped at the hub: duel versus crowd. It reuses the data ideas in resources/weapons/ruler_blade.tres.

skills.name: Pencil Thrust (First Move)
skills.chess_meaning: A pawn's opening privilege is a two-square advance on its first move. The pawn keeps the double reach but turns it into an attack.
skills.rule: Slot: skill_a (Q, project.godot:69). Shape: the two cells in front [facing x1, facing x2]; hits every Health entity in either cell (pierce). Damage 1. impact_delay 0.11 s, recovery 0.52 s (resources/attacks/pencil_thrust.tres). Cooldown 1.25 s starting at cast (scripts/ecs/components/combat_component.gd:12). Shares the attack lock with the Sword. Limiter: straight line only, no diagonals. Interactions: a miss leaves 0.52 s of exposure; an Armed Pawn uses the same two-cell lane, so duels at range 2 are even. Page 'Armed Pawn' lets Q be pressed in the last 0.20 s of Sword recovery.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: Spacing. Two cells away in a straight line is a cell no unarmed Pawn (diagonals), Knight (L cells) or Bishop (diagonals) threatens, so you can poke for free if you read the lane; but a miss costs 0.52 s, and Armed Pawns contest the same lane. It also hits tack-switches across a one-cell hole.
skills.unlocked_where: T4_BrokenRuleYard: the Armed Pawn pokes you from 2 cells first, then a PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=pencil_thrust sits beyond it (revealed on room clear, the same event that unlocks the exit). About minute 12. Optional for the critical path (gp7 calls Pencil optional, gp7-progression-pacing-spec.md:16).
skills.story_beat: Defiance. Black cheated with toys (Act 1 flow map); taking one back is the pawn's first deliberate breaking of 'a piece uses only its own move'.
skills.upgrades: Annotation 'Lead Tip' (optional Toybox room): the first target hit is shoved 1 cell back if free (spacing, not damage). Page 'Armed Pawn' (Margin 1): Sword-to-Pencil chain window. No numeric upgrades.

skills.name: Rule Step (the Knight's Leap)
skills.chess_meaning: Borrowed from the Knight, the only piece that jumps: two cells one way, one cell sideways, ignoring what lies between.
skills.rule: Slot: skill_b (new input action, F). Press F: ghost marks show the two forward L cells in the pawn's facing frame, (2 ahead, 1 left) and (2 ahead, 1 right); tap left or right within 0.15 s to choose, else the free one (right if both are free). Takeoff 0.08 s; flight 0.22 s during which the pawn is untargetable (Status.untargetable_left; HealthSystem ignores damage events for it); the landing cell is reserved at takeoff with the same reserve-then-commit protocol as steps (scripts/ecs/systems/movement_system.gd:38-41); recovery 0.25 s (no step or strike); cooldown 4.0 s from cast ('rare escape, not constant dash', v2:689). Passes over entities, one-cell gaps and blocks tagged leapable; cannot cross room walls, gates or exits. Landing must be free and in bounds. If the landing cell is inside a currently locked telegraph (enemy_ai_system.gd:233,270) the ghost turns red and the pawn is hit on touchdown. Facing is preserved.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: When to leave and where to land. Because enemies lock their cells at telegraph start and test them at resolve, a committed attack can be dodged by relocating over the very obstacles that made stepping impossible (pinned by toy track and wall, boxed in by two pawns). With a 4 s cooldown there is one escape per exchange: spend it early to claim a Knight's landing cell, or save it for the next lock. It also redefines a 'safe cell' because L cells become reachable.
skills.unlocked_where: KB Knight Captain defeated (Toybox), PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=rule_step in the arena after the Black Line lifts. About minute 44. Forced use immediately: the lid shortcut home has a one-cell track gap (v2:649). Hub gate: Dollhouse furniture barricade (Act 1 flow map:502). Do not award it at B1 (Act 1 flow map:464).
skills.story_beat: Freedom beats tradition (v2:285-286). The Book page 'Knight Errant' flips to the amendment 'The Knight may move twice' mid-fight (soulslike plan:130-135) and becomes a Page the pawn can wear. The pawn takes the leap the Knight no longer needs.
skills.upgrades: Annotation 'Full Knight' (optional Bookshelf room): all 8 L cells, including backward. Page 'Knight Errant' (Margin 2): a second Rule Step within 1.0 s of the first, then the full 4.0 s cooldown starts.

skills.name: In Passing (En Passant)
skills.chess_meaning: En passant: a pawn that advances two squares past an enemy pawn may be captured as though it had advanced one; available only on the very next move and only to pawns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/En_passant). The rule becomes the pawn's counter to anything that charges past it.
skills.rule: Granted while Page 'Passant Wraith' (Margin 2) is equipped; no button of its own, it upgrades Strike. Trigger: an enemy completes a move of 2 or more cells (a Charging Pawn, whose movement vectors are two-cell steps, resources/movement/pawn_charging.tres; a Rook charge; the Passant Wraith) that crosses or ends on a cell orthogonally adjacent to the pawn. A chalk 'x' marks the first cell it crossed. For 0.45 s, pressing Strike fires In Passing instead of a Sword swing: zero windup, ignores facing, drags that enemy back to the marked cell if it is free (as though it had moved one cell), 1 damage, 0.8 s stagger that cancels its telegraph and releases the attack token (enemy_ai_system.gd:278-279). One use per window; no cooldown. Does not trigger on Knight leaps (jumps are not passing). The press falls back to a normal Sword swing when no window is open. Data hook: MovementSystem already emits step_started (movement_system.gd:42); add from_cell and cells_crossed to that event for the window.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: Stand beside the lane instead of running out of it. The cell next to a charger's landing point is both the safest and the best attacking cell, so the player reads where the charge will end and waits. Failure is cheap because the press falls back to the Sword.
skills.unlocked_where: Bookshelf Pass (Passant Wraiths in the passages: soulslike plan:145). The Wraith captures you in passing first (amendment 'En passant applies to you', plan:125). After the gauntlet a PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=in_passing flips the Book page; about minute 52. Optional verb: the critical path never requires it, and it respects the vertical-slice limit (gp4:46).
skills.story_beat: A rule used against the pawn becomes the pawn's. It is the only verb that is pawn-only, which keeps the protagonist's identity in a chess war.
skills.upgrades: None as a skill: the window itself is the limiter. An optional later Annotation could widen the trigger to diagonally adjacent cells. Page text may adjust the 0.45 s window.

skills.name: Chalk Path (child call) and Chalk Block
skills.chess_meaning: The child bends the board: a cell that does not exist for the pawn becomes legal. Thematically the Bishop's district (lanes, folded pages): the room can be changed (v2:387-388). The Bishop's lanes are borrowed only as a drawing direction via a Page.
skills.rule: Slot: call (R, v2:135; Tab cycles if two calls). Source: child. Cost 1 Believe segment (max 2; gdd.md:229-235). Cast: press R; a 0.60 s child-hand wind-up appears as a hand shadow over the target cells (enemies and the Queen can disrupt it) and the pawn may move meanwhile. Effect: up to 3 consecutive gap cells in a straight line, starting at the first gap within 3 cells ahead, become walkable chalk for 12 s (6 s in boss arenas, gdd.md:251). Enemies may also walk on it. Rejected with no Believe spent if no gap is within 3 cells or a unit stands on a target cell. Believe never refills by time: +1 per 3 Strike or Pencil hits landed in the current room, +1 per Perfect Rub (Eraser Guard), +1 per rescued-piece reunion, scripted refills at boss phase breaks (gdd.md:231-235). Chalk Block upgrade: the same R on a free floor cell directly ahead raises a Block that stops Rook charges and straight beams until destroyed or room end (gdd.md:243), 1 Believe, max one alive (a new cast moves it), never under a unit.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: Spend or save. Chalk answers geometry (flank across a tear, escape a lane, open a shortcut) while fights you avoid yield no Believe, so help is paid for in courage. The child never kills and never solves a boss phase (gp5:14-18). With Chalk Block the choice becomes bridge versus cover.
skills.unlocked_where: Bookshelf: B3 Torn Page Bridge, the child draws it by script (demonstration), then BB Bishop Oracle defeated; PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=chalk_path; the two-segment Believe HUD appears. About minute 62. Forced use: the shortcut home is a 3-cell page tear. Chalk Block: hub Midpoint after both Bishop and Rook (gdd.md:350-355), unlock_id=chalk_block, about minute 84.
skills.story_beat: Trust. The pawn believes the child is a god (gdd.md:272); the first time the hand is yours to call. At the Midpoint the child admits the war is a story they were playing alone (gdd.md:355).
skills.upgrades: Chalk Block (story, Midpoint). Page 'Bishop of Order' (Margin 2): chalk lasts 18 s and may run diagonally. Page 'Rook Warden' (Margin 3): castling adapted from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castling: R on your Block's row or column with a clear line swaps places with it (0.15 s, 1 Believe).

skills.name: Eraser Guard (Hold the Line)
skills.chess_meaning: The Rook owns straight lines and shields the King in castling (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castling). The pawn borrows the line-defence, but only against lines: an eraser rubs out straight marks, nothing else.
skills.rule: Slot: guard (hold G or left trigger). Raise 0.10 s. While held the pawn is planted (no steps; Shift plus direction turns but re-raises 0.10 s). Negates damage from attacks tagged line (Rook charge, pencil pokes, straight beams) when the attack arrives through the faced cell. Attacks tagged diagonal (Pawn, Bishop) or leap (Knight) ignore the guard, so movement stays mandatory. Perfect Rub: a line attack landing within the first 0.25 s after the guard becomes active puts the attacker In Check: it cannot telegraph or attack for 0.8 s and is pushed back 1 cell if free, and the pawn gains +1 Believe. Early guard is a normal safe block (no bonus); a late guard is no guard. Max hold 1.5 s, then the eraser crumbles for a 0.8 s lockout; no other cooldown. Holding on a Rule Mark floor cell erases it for 6 s (gp5:27, 'Erase Rule Mark'). Hook: damage passes through HealthSystem._apply_damage (health_system.gd:35-50); enemy damage events (enemy_ai_system.gd:271-275) get a tag copied from AttackPattern/EnemyWeapon tags.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: Read the SHAPE of the telegraph and answer with the matching verb: line, plant and hold; diagonal or L, leave. The best defence is the latest safe one, because a Perfect Rub staggers and refills Believe, so defence feeds offence and does not replace movement (https://www.superjumpmagazine.com/the-art-and-science-of-sekiros-combat/, https://tigogardenofmadness.substack.com/p/parrying-action-and-reaction).
skills.unlocked_where: Block Tower: RB Rook Warden defeated, PlayerUnlockMarker unlock_id=eraser_guard; about minute 82. Antepiece: R1/R2 training Rook in a ruler-gated corridor. Forced use: the shortcut gate home needs a rubbed-out Rule Mark. If playtests show RB phase 3 needs it (v2:427 implies this), move the marker to R3 (item-first); that is one node.
skills.story_beat: Standing still can be brave (v2:437). The Book's Rook page records the castling rule. The first time the pawn rubs out a rule instead of dodging it.
skills.upgrades: Annotation 'Rub Out' (optional Block Tower room): the Perfect Rub also clears one active lane telegraph mark of the attacker. Page 'Black Queen' (Margin 3): the 0.25 s Perfect Rub window also rubs out diagonal-tagged hits. No numeric upgrades.

skills.name: Free Step (the Final Rule Break)
skills.chess_meaning: A pawn may CAPTURE diagonally but never MOVE diagonally. Free Step is the pawn making the illegal move legal on its own authority. Promotion would turn it into another piece; this keeps it a pawn (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotion_(chess)).
skills.rule: Slot: move modifier, source own, no cost once unlocked. Press two perpendicular direction keys within 0.06 s (or a diagonal stick): the pawn steps one cell diagonally with the same 0.18 s step and reserve-then-commit protocol; it may squeeze between two blockers that touch at a corner; facing becomes the axis of the later key. Staging: (1) At QB (Queen defeated) a scripted one-time diagonal step opens the Black Castle seal while the child nudges the pawn (this is the 'Gentle Nudge', gdd.md:262-266, kept as a scripted beat, not a verb), matching v2:484; (2) at FB phase 3 the Rule Engine strips the pawn to the legal pawn, forward steps only; each rescued piece restores one of left, right, back (up to 3, gdd.md:371,546) and any unrestored direction is returned by the child in phase 4 so nobody is soft-locked; Believe is locked, the child is cut off; (3) the King's rewritten tiles cover every cardinal approach and the single open cell is diagonal: Free Step into it plus a Sword strike is the finishing blow (gdd.md:373). Afterwards Free Step is permanent.
skills.new_decision_it_creates: The only new movement decision in the game that is not a cooldown: it reopens every geometry the player solved with cardinal steps. It arrives only when help is gone, so the question becomes how to use complete freedom.
skills.unlocked_where: Under-Bed Black Castle, FB Black King, phases 3-4; about minute 108. Ending: the Last Rank promotion prompt follows. Gauntlet rooms F1/F2 re-test each earlier verb first.
skills.story_beat: The courage to disobey now belongs to the pawn (gdd.md:272); the pawn refuses promotion and steps beyond the board (gdd.md:377-380).
skills.upgrades: None. After the finale it reopens diagonal gaps (for example the Dollhouse barricade) as optional exploration.

proposed_progression.other_growth:
All growth is data and story-gated; none is grindable.

COURAGE (health): fixed at 3 for tuning, as in the GDD (gdd.md:131). Optional Courage Shards (crayon-blue) sit in verb-gated spots: hub (Pencil tack-switch), Toybox (Rule Step gap), Bookshelf (Chalk bridge), Block Tower (Guard erases a Rule Mark), Dollhouse (Rule Step over barricade), Under-Bed F1 (Chalk Block); 3 shards = +1 max Courage, capped at 5. Modelled on heart pieces that sit behind obstacles you pass later (https://www.zeldadungeon.net/wiki/Link's_Awakening_Heart_Pieces, search summary). Tune every boss for 3 Courage and treat shards as a soft assist for explorers.

BELIEVE (child economy): max 2 segments, fixed. Earned by hits landed, Perfect Rub and rescues; never by time. Scripted refills at boss phase breaks.

RANK and MARGIN: rank 2 + defeated bosses; Margin = rank - 1 (2, 3, 4, 5, 6 across the five non-final bosses).

RULE PAGES (equippable, from the existing Book of House Rules; each is a RuleEntry .tres extended with margin_cost and a modifier list; pages are rule changes, not stat bumps): The First Law (Pawn Recruit) cost 0, lore only. Armed Pawn cost 1: Q may chain from the last 0.20 s of Sword recovery. Backstep Pawn cost 1: a step directly away from the faced cell after a Strike cancels the rest of Sword recovery. Charging Pawn cost 1: after standing still 1.0 s the next step covers 2 cells if both are free (the First-Move Charge). Knight Errant cost 2: Rule Step may chain once within 1.0 s. Passant Wraith cost 2: grants In Passing. Bishop of Order cost 2: Chalk lasts 18 s and may run diagonally. Promoted Zealot cost 2: at 1 Courage, post-hit invulnerability extends from 0.70 s to 1.20 s ('forgets fear', soulslike plan:127). Rook Warden cost 3: Castling swap with your Chalk Block. Black Queen cost 3: Perfect Rub also rubs out diagonal hits. Ten pages against a maximum Margin of 6: the owner can ship five (the five already in resources/rules/) and add the rest as districts land.

PAGE UNLOCK RULE: a page unlocks when its piece is first met (existing behaviour) and becomes equippable once its owner is beaten or its lesson passed; the Knight page flips mid-fight and is wearable after (soulslike plan:130-135).

ANNOTATIONS (skill upgrades): permanent, free, rule-changing, found in one optional room per district: Lead Tip, Full Knight, Rub Out. They are SkillUpgrade lists inside SkillDef, so no new type.

RESCUED PIECES: up to three optional white pieces (gdd.md:546). Each restores 1 Courage at its safe spot (gdd.md:134), restores one direction in the finale (gdd.md:371), adds a Believe refill, and varies the ending shot. This gives relatedness, the third motivation need (https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/SDT/documents/2006_RyanRigbyPrzybylski_MandE.pdf, search summary).

HUB EVOLUTION: visible progress, not stats: shelter after Knight, banners after Bishop, toy train after Rook, gathering at the chess box after Queen (gdd.md:303-310).

TOY WEAPONS: the Sword is the default Strike; the Ruler Blade is an optional swap. No weapon levels.

CHILD TRUST STATES: story flags in WorldState drive the child's lines and the HUD marks.

NOT INCLUDED: XP, currency, shops, inventory grids, stat upgrades (gdd.md:554; soulslike plan:96-97). Optional later: negative-cost Vow pages for harder play (positive/negative pairs as in Shotgun King: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_King:_The_Final_Checkmate, search summary) and gp5 calls not built (Turn the Board, Hold Ruler Gate, Paper Bridge), each of which would be one SkillDef plus a room marker, with one new effect kind for Turn the Board.
proposed_progression.difficulty_curve:
Model: perceived difficulty = (skill challenge + power challenge) - (player skill + player power) (https://gamebalanceconcepts.wordpress.com/2010/08/18/level-7-advancement-progression-and-pacing/). Player POWER is deliberately flat, so the curve is controlled with the other terms: enemy shape count and telegraph timing (data), player SKILL (taught by the verb cycle) and option space (verbs, Pages). Power challenge stays nearly flat as well: normal enemies 2-3 HP (soulslike plan:158), Captain 4 (resources/enemies/black_pawn_captain.tres), Knight 12 with a phase shift at 6 (plan:159); suggested start values for later bosses 12, 14, 16, 18, to be tuned by the boss lane.

SAWTOOTH per district (Schreiber): difficulty jumps on entry, plateaus, spikes at the boss; then a trough room (rest, story, a safe first use of the new verb) and a small power jump (new verb, Page, Margin +1). Minutes are targets from docs/design/gp7-progression-pacing-spec.md:14-22.

min 0-6, T1-T2, rank 2: Step, Turn, Sword. 0 threat shapes. Target: nobody dies.
min 6-12, T3-T4, rank 2: Pencil (12). 1 shape (pawn diagonal). Median player loses at most 1 Courage per room.
min 12-25, B1 plus H1, rank 2->3: Margin 2, first Pages. 1-2 shapes. B1 median 2 attempts: a small first fiero. Child foreshadow only.
min 25-45, Toybox plus KB, rank 3->4: Charging Pawn page, Rule Step (44). 2 shapes (L plus diagonal), Knight telegraph 0.9 s. KB median 3 attempts.
min 45-65, Bookshelf plus BB, rank 4->5: In Passing page (52), Chalk (62). 2 shapes (diagonal lane plus pawn). BB median 3.
min 65-85, Block Tower plus RB, rank 5->6: Eraser Guard (82), Midpoint Chalk Block (84). 2 shapes (line plus pawn), 3 in phase 3. RB median 3-4.
min 85-105, Dollhouse plus QB, rank 6->7: Queen page, scripted diagonal. 3 shapes (Queen mix); phase 3 locks Believe so the pawn acts alone. QB median 4.
min 105-120, Under-Bed, FB, ending, rank 7->8: Free Step. 3-4 shapes with tile rewrites. FB median 5-6 attempts; Last Rank prompt.

MICRO-REWARDS (every 5 minutes or so): Page, Annotation, Courage Shard, rescue, hub change. They keep the long gap between the Pencil (12) and Rule Step (44) from feeling empty.

FLOW AND FAIRNESS: static difficulty fits few players (Chen, https://cacm.acm.org/magazines/2007/4/5692-flow-in-games-and-everything-else/fulltext, search summary). Valves, all existing data: DifficultyProfile multipliers (telegraph, observe, recovery, movement: scripts/data/difficulty_profile.gd:5-8), assist options (telegraph x1.25 or x1.5, slow enemies while stationary: gdd.md:524-533), Courage Shards, Pages. Upward valve: Vow pages. Celeste's lesson is to offer in-between assist options and explain them plainly (https://www.vice.com/en/article/celeste-difficulty-assist-mode/, search summary). Fiero needs real failure followed by triumph (Lazzaro, https://yukaichou.com/behavioral-design/4-keys-2-fun-part-1-4/), so cap boss attempts: after about 8 deaths on one boss, offer assist once.

DEATH: unchanged (zone reload; world state persists; plan:94). Runbacks stay short (plan:78-80).
proposed_progression.reconcile_with_owner_history:
The owner cut XP leveling, bonfires and corpse-run on 2026-07-28 (docs/soulslike-world-plan.md:4-8, 96-97). This proposal reintroduces none of them: no XP or levels, no currency, no checkpoints, no corpse-run; death keeps today's zone reload. Rank is a label for defeated bosses, not a level; the plan's cut idea named 'Promotion leveling' is a different thing from the Last Rank promotion prompt, but the name collision should be avoided in UI (use 'Rank' in the HUD and never 'level'). Margin is derived from rank, so there is nothing to grind. gdd.md:554 excludes 'statistical weapon upgrades' and shops; Pages are limited to rule changes and ship with Book text, and the Book of House Rules itself is the owner's own mechanism (plan:99-114). Courage Shards are the only numeric growth and are optional.

Where this departs from approved or proposed text, flagged for an owner decision:
1) docs/design/gdd.md:112-115 (June, approved concept) says one toy weapon plus up to two Imagination skills in loadout slots. Proposal: fixed verbs on dedicated buttons, with the loadout moved to Pages; five verbs in two slots would make forced-teaching rooms impossible. Keeping two slots is a data setting (slot_count).
2) gdd.md:326-364 (approved) gives rewards Place Block (Knight), Draw Path (Bishop), Turn the Board (Rook), Gentle Nudge (Queen). docs/design/gp4-skill-system-spec.md:21-29 and full-gameplay-design-v2.md:581-590 (drafts for review) give Rule Step, Chalk Path, Eraser Guard, Final Rule Break. The proposal follows gp4/v2 (own-rule chain, vertical slice of Sword, Pencil, Rule Step per gp4:46) but keeps the child's Draw Path, merges Place Block into Chalk Block, keeps Gentle Nudge as the scripted seed of Free Step, and defers Turn the Board as an extension. The child still places a block for the pawn once, by script, in Toybox, preserving gdd.md:330.
3) Final Rule Break: v2:484 puts it at the Queen; gp7:22 puts it at the King. Proposal: scripted use at the Queen (castle seal), player-owned Free Step at the King.
4) Boss order: gdd.md:294-299 allows Bishop and Rook in either order; v2 is linear. The proposal supports either order because each district needs only earlier verbs.
5) Unlock timing: gp4/gp7 grant at the boss; v2:427 implies Guard is needed during the Rook fight. Placement is one node, so playtests decide.
6) Promotion: the GDD and the v2 recommended answer keep the pawn a pawn (gdd.md:377; v2:795). The proposal adds a prompt that offers promotion and lets the player decline, which needs one UI screen and one event (last_rank_reached).
7) Act 1 stays free of major skills (Act 1 flow map:60-66,464); only Sword and the optional Pencil appear before the Knight.

Ending fidelity: the ending still shows the pawn stepping beyond the board (gdd.md:380), the child rebuilding the playground (gdd.md:379), and rescue-based variations (gdd.md:547).
